## Background

This Protection Profile (PP) is developed based on Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (eIDAS 2.0), and Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2981.

This PP defines the Wallet Instance (WI) as the Target of Evaluation WI-(TOE) for the Remote HSM configuration of a European Digital Identity Wallet. In this configuration, the Wallet Instance operates on the user device and interacts with the WSCA running on Wallet Provider backend infrastructure, which in turn uses a certified remote HSM as the WSCD. The Wallet Instance provides security-relevant functionality including user authentication and authorization, protection of Wallet Unit data and device-resident security assets, and secure interaction with the WSCA/WSCD for security-sensitive operations.

This PP specifies the functional and assurance security requirements for the Wallet Instance within the FITCEM certification framework. It is intended to provide a common security baseline for evaluating the Wallet Instance as part of an EUDI Wallet using the Remote HSM architecture, including its security dependencies and interactions with the WSCA/WSCD.

## Terminology

This Protection Profile uses the terminology defined in the European Digital Identity Wallet Architecture and Reference Framework (ARF) and the applicable EU regulations. Unless otherwise stated, terms such as Wallet Unit, Wallet Instance, Wallet Secure Cryptographic Application (WSCA), Wallet Secure Cryptographic Device (WSCD), Wallet Provider, Wallet User, Wallet Instance Attestation (WIA), Key Attestation (KA), and critical assets shall have the meaning defined in the ARF and the applicable Commission Implementing Regulations.

Where this Protection Profile introduces terms specific to the Remote HSM architecture, these terms are explicitly defined in this Protection Profile. In case of ambiguity, the definitions in the applicable EU legislation take precedence over terminology introduced in this Protection Profile. The following terms defining the secure authentication protocol between the Wallet Instance and the WSCA/WSCD are specific to the Remote HSM architecture:

- Remote User Authentication Protocol (RUAP): The protocol enforces that every PIN verification is performed through a live and fresh interaction between the Wallet Instance and the WSCA. This ensures that the confidentiality of the PIN is preserved, while verification is subject to controlled and rate limited processing at the WSCA. The Wallet Instance must demonstrate the User Authentication Evidence (UAE), which is derived both from a knowledge-based factor (derived from the PIN) and a possessionbased factor. The User Authentication Evidence (UAE) is verified against the Authentication Reference Data (ARD) which is shared during enrolment.
- Authentication Reference Data (ARD): Authentication Reference Data is shared with the WSCA/WSCD during enrolment and used at the WSCA/WSCD to verify the Authentication Reference Data (UAE).
- User Authentication Evidence (UAE) Cryptographic evidence bound to a user authentication event at the wallet instance, provided over the Remote Authentication Channel and verified by the WSCA before it performs a wallet cryptographic operation. •

This Protection Profile is intended to be used within the legal, regulatory, certification and technical framework established by the following documents and standards.

### 1.2 TOE Overview {#s-1-2}

The Target of Evaluation (TOE) is a European Digital Identity Wallet Instance (here after is abbreviated by WI-(TOE)) is a mobile application designed to give users full control over how they manage and share their personal identity. The WI-(TOE) securely stores official identification data and supporting credentials from authorized PID /Attestation Providers. It lets individuals present these credentials to verified service providers for both online interactions and in-person checks using common standards. By supporting selective disclosure, the app ensures people can share only the specific information required for a service without exposing extraneous details, all while maintaining privacy and offering a straightforward way to sign documents digitally.

The TOE is designed exclusively for a remote HSM configuration, in which the securitycritical cryptographic assets and operations are managed by a remotely deployed Wallet Secure Cryptographic Device (WSCD) accessed through the Wallet Secure Cryptographic Application (WSCA).

#### 1.2.1 The WI- (TOE) in the Wallet ecosystem {#s-1-2-1}

The Wallet Instance, WI-(TOE), is one of the components in the Wallet Unit, which acts as part of the Wallet ecosystem. In Figure 1 the main components of the Wallet Unit and wallet ecosystem are depicted.

Figure 1 — Wallet Unit as part of the Wallet Ecosystem

![Image](/img/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/nl-cs-wi/image_000000_9ccb3826718d121ca478815afcddac6e5e0733d8988b064a2b04797a57f41fc0.png)

#### 1.2.2 Wallet Unit components {#s-1-2-2}

The following components are the core components in the Wallet Unit, as depicted in Figure 1:

- User device (UD): The hardware, operating system and software environment on which the Wallet Instance executes. The User Device provides the execution environment and local security mechanisms used to protect the Wallet Instance, User authentication and local data. Its security posture, including the integrity of the operating system and relevant security mechanisms, contributes to the overall security of the Wallet Unit.
- Wallet Instance (WI-(TOE)): The mobile application installed on the User Device. The WI-(TOE) authenticates ecosystem entities, obtains User approval for securitysensitive actions, manages credentials and cryptographic assets, and initiates cryptographic operations. It shall protect sensitive Wallet Unit information and ensure that security-sensitive operations are performed only under the applicable authorization and User-control conditions. It interfaces with one or more key stores for the management of non-critical cryptographic assets.
- Wallet Secure Cryptographic Application (WSCA): A WSCA implementation deployed on a hardened backend server. It provides security-critical cryptographic functionality and interfaces with the WSCD. The WSCA enforces the applicable security controls for cryptographic operations and ensures that operations involving critical assets are performed only after the required authorization and User authentication conditions have been satisfied.
- Wallet Secure Cryptographic Device (WSCD): A hardware security device used by the WSCA to protect critical cryptographic assets and perform security-sensitive cryptographic operations. The WSCD shall protect the confidentiality and integrity of protected private keys and shall prevent unauthorized export or use of protected private keys.
- Keystore User Device (Keystore): An applicable hardware-backed SE used to generate, store and use cryptographic assets that are not required to be protected by the WSCD. The possession factor used by the authentication protocol is managed in the

keystore. The keystore shall provide the security level appropriate to the assets it protects and prevent unauthorized access to the associated private keys.

#### 1.2.3 Wallet ecosystem entities {#s-1-2-3}

The following entities (depicted in Figure Figure 1) are part Wallet Ecosystem and interact with the Wallet Unit:

- Wallet Provider Backend (WPB): Provides Wallet Provider services, including Wallet Unit onboarding, activation, management, maintenance and security-status related services. The Wallet Provider is responsible for establishing the required trust relationship with the Wallet Instance, issuing the WIA and KA, and taking appropriate action when the security or trustworthiness of a Wallet Unit is compromised.
- PID and Attestation Providers: Providers that issue PIDs and Attestations to the Wallet Unit. Before issuance, the Provider authenticates the Wallet Unit and verifies the applicable WIA and KA, including their validity and revocation status. For device-bound credentials, the Provider verifies proof-of-possession of the private key corresponding to the public key contained in the KA and binds the issued credential to that key.
- Relying Parties (RPs): Entities that request and verify PID or Attestation attributes from the Wallet Unit to provide a service to the User. The RP authenticates to the Wallet Unit using the applicable Access Certificate and provides the information required for the User to understand and approve the requested disclosure. The RP is responsible for verifying the authenticity, integrity, freshness and applicable cryptographic binding of the received presentation.
- Access Certificate Infrastructure: Provides Access Certificates used to authenticate relevant ecosystem entities. The associated trust infrastructure provides the trust anchors required by the Wallet Unit and other ecosystem participants to verify the authenticity of Access Certificates.

#### 1.2.4 Principal security interactions {#s-1-2-4}

The principal high level data flows and trust relationships are as follows between the entities:

- Wallet Instance (WI-(TOE)) – WSCA: The Wallet Instance communicates with the WSCA through a protected channel. User authentication and the Remote User Authentication Protocol (RUAP), including User Authentication Evidence (UAE) and Authentication Reference Data (ARD), are used to authorize security-sensitive operations. The WSCA invokes the WSCD for operations involving protected cryptographic assets. Per-key authentication shall be implemented at the WSCD and the per-key authorization data shall secure stored by the WI-(TOE).
- Wallet Instance (WI-(TOE)) – PID/Attestation Providers: The Wallet Instance communicates with the Provider to request and receive PIDs or Attestations. Where required, the Wallet Unit provides the applicable WIA and KA. The Provider verifies these objects and may request proof-of-possession of the corresponding private keys before issuing a device-bound credential.
- Wallet Instance (WI-(TOE)) – Relying Party: The Wallet Instance participates in credential presentation using the applicable presentation protocol. It authenticates the Relying Party, evaluates the presentation request, obtains explicit User approval and performs selective disclosure. For device-bound credentials, the Wallet Unit uses the applicable WSCA/WSCD to perform the required cryptographic operation and proof-ofpossession.
- Wallet Instance (WI-(TOE)) - Keystore User Device: The Wallet Instance uses applicable keystores to generate, store and use cryptographic assets in accordance with their required security level. The Wallet Instance shall ensure that operations involving

protected assets are subject to the applicable User authentication and authorization controls.

- Wallet Instance (WI-(TOE)) - Wallet Provider backend (WPB): The Wallet Instance communicates with the Wallet Provider for installation, onboarding, activation, Wallet Unit management and security-status related services. During onboarding and activation, the Wallet Provider receives the attested keys and the WIA key material, as applicable, and securely shares WIA and KA with the WI-(TOE).

The security relationships described above establish the principal boundaries of the Wallet Unit and its interactions with the EUDI Wallet ecosystem. Section 1.3 describes the Wallet Unit lifecycle and the cryptographic trust relationship between the Wallet Instance, WIA, KA, WSCA/WSCD, PIDs, Attestations and Relying Parties. It provides the basis for the subsequent Security Problem Definition and security requirements. The complete set of Functional Security Requirements (FSRs) applicable to the WI-(TOE) is specified in section 3.1.

#### 1.2.5 The WI-(TOE) User Device Protection and Self Protection {#s-1-2-5}

The WI-(TOE) is executed on top of a mobile user device, and therefore strongly depend for its security operation on the security measures from the mobile operating system and the mobile hardware.

The WI-(TOE) however shall properly implement this self-protection mechanisms and make appropriate use of the security features provided by the mobile operating system and underlying mobile hardware. These requirements are explicitly defined as part of the Resilience Security Requirements (RSRs) in section 3.2. In this section a summary of the expected security measures is provided.

The WI-(TOE) shall securely utilize the following mobile operating system level protections mechanisms:

- Application sandboxing: isolates the Wallet Instance and its data from other applications.
- Access control and permissions: controls access to sensitive device resources such as NFC, camera, biometrics, and storage.
- Secure storage APIs: provides protected storage for sensitive wallet data and cryptographic material.
- Keystore/key-management services: allows the wallet to generate and use cryptographic keys without exposing private key material directly to the application.
- User authentication: enables wallet operations or key usage to be gated by a device PIN, password, or biometric authentication.
- Application integrity and signing: ensures that installed applications originate from an unmodified signed package.
- Secure communication interfaces: provides OS-controlled networking and IPC mechanisms that limit unauthorized access between applications and services.

The WI-TOE shall securely utilize the security services provided by the platform's Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) and/or Secure Element (SE). These trusted components shall provide the following security mechanisms:

- Non-exportable hardware-backed key generation, ensuring that cryptographic keys are generated and remain protected within the TEE or SE and cannot be exported in plaintext form.
- Protected cryptographic operations, whereby sensitive cryptographic operations are performed within the trusted environment, without exposing private key material to the Rich Execution Environment (REE) or to the Wallet Instance.

- Hardware-enforced key usage policies, restricting the use of protected keys to authorized algorithms, operations, and purposes.
- Resistance to key extraction, achieved through hardware and logical isolation mechanisms that provide significantly stronger protection against key disclosure than application-level storage.
- Key and device attestation, enabling the platform to provide cryptographic evidence regarding the characteristics of the protected keys, the integrity of the device, and the security properties of the TEE or SE in which the keys are protected.

The WI-(TOE) shall implement self-protection mechanisms to maintain its confidentiality, integrity, authenticity and privacy when operating in a potentially hostile mobile environment. These mechanisms shall include:

- Security monitoring and reporting, including the detection and reporting to the Wallet Provider of tampering attempts and insecure platform states.
- Protection against debugging, including the absence of production debug functionality and debug artefacts, and the detection of attached debuggers.
- Platform-state verification, including the detection of rooted, jailbroken, emulated, virtualised, developer/debug-mode or otherwise insecure operating environments, and the disabling of security-critical functionality when such a state is detected.
- Secure use of platform security mechanisms, including application isolation, mandatory access controls and hardware-backed security services.
- Protection of sensitive assets, including secure key management, approved cryptographic services, secure random number generation, encrypted storage, secure transmission and secure memory clearing.
- Secure application design and implementation, following secure coding practices and protecting against common mobile application security threats.
- User interface and sensitive-operation protection, including protection of PIN entry and sensitive screens against screen capture, overlay and tapjacking attacks, accessibility-service abuse, malware-assisted attacks and unauthorised exposure of sensitive information.
- Privacy protection, ensuring that personal data is processed in a transparent and privacy-preserving manner and that user tracking is prevented.

In addition, the WI-(TOE) may implement the following best-practice hardening mechanisms. Where implemented, they shall meet the corresponding Resilience Security Requirements:

- Code and resource obfuscation, including anti-deobfuscation measures, to hinder reverse engineering of security-sensitive functionality.
- Protection against runtime instrumentation, including the detection of or resistance to code injection, function hooking, API interception and dynamic analysis.
- TOE integrity verification, including periodic verification of the integrity and authenticity of the TOE’s code and security-relevant resources.
- Device attestation, providing authenticated and fresh evidence of the security state of the User Device.
- Application-level payload encryption, in addition to transport-layer protection.
- Protection against loss of user-interface focus during security-sensitive interactions.

### 1.3 Wallet Unit Lifecycle and Cryptographic Trust Relationships {#s-1-3}

The WI-(TOE) forms part of a Wallet Unit within the EUDI Wallet ecosystem. This section provides context for the security and trust relationships established during the Wallet Unit lifecycle.

It describes how the Wallet Instance interacts with the Wallet Provider, WSCA/WSCD, keystores, PID and Attestation Providers, and Relying Parties, and how cryptographic mechanisms are used to establish authenticity, integrity, confidentiality and cryptographic binding where required.

This section distinguishes between trust established through cryptographic mechanisms and trust established through certification, registration, trusted lists and other ecosystem governance mechanisms.

#### 1.3.1 Wallet Instance Installation {#s-1-3-1}

The Wallet Instance should preferably be distributed through an official application distribution channel of the User Device operating system. If the Wallet Instance is distributed through another mechanism, the Wallet Provider shall provide a mechanism enabling the User to verify the authenticity and integrity of the Wallet Instance before installation.

##### 1.3.1.1 Mutual Authentication Channel {#s-1-3-1-1}

After installation, the Wallet Instance establishes the required secure communication channels with:

- the Wallet Provider; and
- the WSCA/WSCD

Communication between the Wallet Instance and Wallet Provider shall provide mutual authentication and shall provide confidentiality and integrity protection where required.

##### 1.3.1.2 Initial Data Requested by Wallet Provider {#s-1-3-1-2}

The WI-(TOE) will now send its initial data to the Wallet Provider which contains technical data from the Wallet Instance, including cryptographic and hardware capabilities (such as WSCD and keystore details), system diagnostics (including OS, SDK, and library versions, plus information about available communication interfaces such as BLE and NFC), and security posture signals such as rooting, emulator, and malware detection.

The Wallet Provider shall limit collected device and security-posture information to the data necessary for Wallet Solution deployment, maintenance and security-posture monitoring. Collection shall be minimised and performed with appropriate privacy safeguards.

#### 1.3.2 Wallet Activation {#s-1-3-2}

For Wallet Activation, the following steps are performed:

- Creation of a Wallet Provider user account and association of the Wallet Instance with that account (further detailed in section 1.3.2.1).
- Registration of the User authentication methods that will be used to access and operate the wallet (further detailed in section 1.3.2.2).
- Initial Generation and issuance of the WIA and KA (further detailed in section 1.3.2.3)

During activation, the Wallet Provider establishes the required trust relationship with the Wallet Instance and provides the WIA and KA required for subsequent Wallet Unit operations. The WIA provides information about the Wallet Instance and Wallet Solution, while the KA provides information about the WSCA/WSCD and the public keys used by the Wallet Unit.

The User authentication mechanisms established during activation are subsequently used to control access to the Wallet Unit and, where applicable, to protect security-sensitive cryptographic operations involving critical Wallet Unit assets.

The following sections describe the individual activation steps and the associated cryptographic assets.

##### 1.3.2.1 Wallet Provider User account {#s-1-3-2-1}

The User must register with the Wallet Provider to create a Wallet Provider User account. The wallet provider must associate the User account with the installed Wallet Instance.

The Wallet Provider associates the Wallet Unit with a User account to support Wallet Unit management, including User-requested revocation. The account does not necessarily need to contain the User's real-world identity unless required for a specific Wallet function or legal obligation.

##### 1.3.2.2 User Authentications {#s-1-3-2-2}

The User enrols two user authentication mechanisms to the Wallet Instance. These two User authentication mechanisms are:

## OS-level User authentication:

- The Wallet Instance shall require OS-level User authentication whenever the Wallet Instance is opened and before performing Wallet Unit operations. The OS-level authentication mechanism shall use possession of the User Device together with a knowledge-based or inherence-based factor.
- This local OS-based authentication shall be enforced at startup of the WI-(TOE) and before security-sensitive actions, such as
    - generating and presenting pseudonyms,
    - accessing the transaction log via the dashboard,
    - requesting the erasure of personal data by a Relying Party;
    - other operations as specified by the applicable ARF requirements.

## WSCA/WSCD-level Remote User Authentication Protocol (RUAP):

- This specific Remote User Authentication Protocol (RUAP), including the use of User Authentication Evidence (UAE) and Authentication Reference Data (ARD), is a PP-specific mechanism defined to implement the required WSCA/WSCD-level User authentication.
- The RUAP shall support User authentication meeting the applicable requirements for Level of Assurance High as specified in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1502. In particular, the authentication mechanism shall use at least two authentication factors from different categories and shall implement security controls such that guessing, eavesdropping, replay and manipulation of the authentication communication cannot, with high attack potential, subvert the authentication mechanism.
- The Wallet Instance WI-(TOE) must demonstrate the User Authentication Evidence (UAE), which is derived both from a knowledge-based authentication factor (derived from the PIN) and a possession-based authentication factor, which are jointly validated to achieve two-factor authentication and to prevent manipulation or forged attempts.
- Remote User Authentication Protocol (RUAP) ensure PIN Verification and ensure that the User has sole control over the critical assets located in the WSCD, such that these assets cannot be used without the User's involvement through the required authentication factors;

- The protocol protects the confidentiality and integrity of the authentication data during PIN verification and enrolment, and provides protection against duplication, tampering, eavesdropping and replay attacks, including through freshness and challenge binding;
- Each PIN verification is performed through a live and fresh interaction between the WI(TOE) and the WSCA/WSCD, preventing reuse of previously exchanged authentication information;
- During enrolment, the Wallet Instance WI-(TOE) ensures that both the knowledge and possession factors are securely initialized and cryptographically bound to the Authentication Reference Data (ARD). Authentication Reference Data (ARD) is derived and is shared with the WSCA /WSCD during initial enrolment. This binding preserves confidentiality and integrity of the knowledge-based authentication factor (derived from the PIN) and a possession-based authentication factor and prevents compromise also if the confidentiality of the Authentication Reference Data (ARD) is not preserved.
- A Personal Unblocking Key (PUK) can be integrated in the protocol to reset the knowledge-based factor in case the PIN was forgotten.
- Per-key authentication data shall be sent to the Wallet Instance WI-(TOE) and be provided at every security-sensitive cryptographic operation of the applicable key, to ensure sole control of the Wallet User before the execution by the WSCD.
- This authentication mechanism is subsequently required whenever the Wallet Unit performs cryptographic operations involving protected assets within the WSCA/WSCD, ensuring that all such operations remain securely bound to both the user and the user device. At a minimum, in the following situations. WSCA/WSCD-level User Authentication is required:
    - Initial Generation of KAs and WIA (further detailed in section 1.3.2.3).
    - The Wallet Unit asks the User for approval of selective disclosure to a Relying Party (further detailed in section 1.3.4.2)
    - The User deletes a PID or attestation in their Wallet Unit (further detailed in section 1.3.4.3).
    - The User instructs the Wallet to request the issuance of a new PID or Attestation.

##### 1.3.2.3 Initial Generation of the WIA and KA {#s-1-3-2-3}

During Wallet Activation, at least one set of Wallet Unit Attestations (WUA) is issued. These attestations comprise the Key Attestation(s) (KA) and the Wallet Instance Attestation (WIA).

The KA provides information about the WSCA/WSCD and contains the cryptographic public keys of the attested key pairs. The corresponding private keys are protected by the WSCA/WSCD. The WIA provides information about the Wallet Instance and Wallet Solution, including applicable certification information. The WIA device-binding key pair may optionally be generated within the WSCA/WSCD or managed within the context of the Wallet Instance.

The WIA and KA are issued and signed by the Wallet Provider after the Wallet Provider has performed the applicable verification of the Wallet Instance and cryptographic environment.

###### 1.3.2.3.1 Key attestations (KA) {#s-1-3-2-3-1}

The User must perform WSCA/WSCD-level user authentication through the TOE to request the WSCA/WSCD to generate the attested keys for the Key Attestation (KA). The Key Attestation (KA) is a signed information object, generated and signed using the Wallet Provider signing key (WP\_SIG\_PRIV1), and contains:

- One or more attested public keys (PID/ATT\_PUB\_KEYs)
- Applicable certification and security information concerning the WSCA/WSCD.

The attested public keys (PID/ATT\_PUB\_KEYs) shall be securely transferred from the WSCA/WSCD to the Wallet Provider during KA issuance.

Key Attestation (KA) has the following purposes:

- The Wallet Unit shares the KA with the PID and Attestation Providers during issuance of a device-bound PID or Attestation.
- PID Provider or an Attestation Provider verify the signature using the WP\_SIG\_PUB1, verified through a certificate chain, where the Provider’s certificate is validated through the Access Certificate Authority (ACA) up to a trusted anchor provisioned by the relevant EUDI Wallet trust framework.
- PID Provider or an Attestation Provider will use the Applicable certification and security information of the WSCA/WSCD, to verify if the WSCA/WSCD is fit to protect the private keys for a PID or Attestation or whether it is revoked.
- PID Provider or an Attestation Provider can request a proof-of-possession, by sending a nonce via the wallet instance to the WSCA/WSCD to be signed with private keys (PID/ATT\_PRIV\_KEYs) corresponding to PID/ATT\_PUB\_KEYs. This proves that the (PID/ATT\_PRIV\_KEYs) corresponding to PID/ATT\_PUB\_KEYs are generated by and stored in the WSCA/WSCD.
- PID Provider or an Attestation Provider will include the PID/ATT\_PUB\_KEYs the issued PID or Attestation.

###### 1.3.2.3.2 Wallet Instance Attestation (WIA) {#s-1-3-2-3-2}

The Wallet Instance Attestation (WIA) is a signed information object, signed by the Wallet Provider Key (WP\_SIG\_PRIV2) and contains:

- Wallet Information: Wallet Solution ID/Name, version and URIs with Certification information and additional Wallet Solution information.
- Expiration and revocation status. The technical validity period of a WIA shall be less than 24 hours.
- WIA public key: WIA\_KEY\_PUB.

The WIA device-binding key pair (WIA\_KEY\_PRIV and WIA\_KEY\_PUB) may be managed either by the WSCA/WSCD or by the Instance. Where managed by the Wallet instance, the private key shall be adequately protected against unauthorised access, disclosure, modification, and use. Where managed by the WSCA/WSCD, the key pair is subject to the security controls and protection mechanisms of the WSCA/WSCD.

The WIA device-binding public key WIA\_KEY\_PUB shall be securely transferred from the Wallet Instance or from the WSCA/WSCD to the Wallet Provider during WIA issuance.

Key Attestation has the following purposes:

- The Wallet Unit shared Wallet Instance Attestation (WIA) with the PID and Attestation Providers.
- PID Provider or an Attestation Provider verify the signature using the WP\_SIG\_PUB2, verified through a certificate chain, where the Provider’s certificate is validated through the Access Certificate Authority (ACA) up to a trusted anchor provisioned by the relevant EUDI Wallet trust framework.
- Sent to PID and Attestation Providers to inform them about the Wallet Instance details, such as Wallet Solution name, version, and certification of the Wallet Solution. This allows the PID or Attestation Provider to verify information about the Wallet Solution and Wallet Instance and to determine whether the associated Wallet Instance is currently revoked. The Wallet Provider performs the applicable integrity verification

before issuing the WIA. The verify if the TOE belongs to a certified Wallet Solution registered in the Wallet Provider Trusted List.

- PID Provider or an Attestation Provider will use the Wallet Identifiers to verify if the TOE belongs to a certified Wallet Solution registered in the Wallet Provider Trusted List.
- PID Provider or an Attestation Provider uses the revocation reference allowing a PID Provider or an Attestation Provider to verify if the Wallet Solution has been revoked.
- PID Provider or an Attestation Provider can request a proof-of-possession, by sending a nonce via the wallet instance to the WSCA/WSCD to be signed with private keys (WIA\_KEY\_PRIV) corresponding to WIA\_KEY\_PUB. This proves that the (WIA\_KEY\_PRIV) corresponding to WIA\_KEY\_PUB is managed by the Wallet Unit.

#### 1.3.3 PID/Attestation Provider authentication and Issuance. {#s-1-3-3}

Before the PID/Attestation Provider issues the PID or the Attestation to the Wallet Unit, they will first authenticate to each other.

##### 1.3.3.1 PID/Attestation Provider authentication to the Wallet Unit {#s-1-3-3-1}

The first step in the issuance process is the authentication of the Provider by the Wallet Instance.

During Provider authentication the TOE executes the following steps:

- TOE initiates connection with the PID/Attestation Provider.
- The Provider returns to the TOE its Access Certificate (ISS\_ACC\_CERT) and, where applicable, a Registration Certificate (ISS\_REG\_CERT).
- The TOE verifies the certificates using the applicable trusted anchor.
- The TOE verifies the Provider's registered identity, role and, where applicable, the credential types or services for which the Provider is registered. This information is obtained from the Registration Certificate or the applicable Registrar service.

##### 1.3.3.2 Wallet Unit authentication to the PID/Attestation Provider {#s-1-3-3-2}

The next step in the Issuance process is for the TOE to send the PID/attestation request (OpenID4VCI -Credential Request) to the Provider, and for the Provider to authenticate the WUAs (KA & WIA).

During WIA authentication the following steps are executed:

- TOE sends the signed WIA to the Provider.
- The Provider verifies the WIA signature using the applicable Wallet Provider public key (WP\_SIG\_PUB2). Trust in the Provider's public key shall be established through the applicable Trust List or LoTE.
- The Provider verifies the validity and revocation status of the WIA.
- The Provider requests proof-of-possession from the Wallet Unit of WIA\_KEY\_PRIV corresponding to WIA\_KEY\_PUB contained in the WIA. The Provider provides a nonce to the TOE. The TOE signs the nonce using WIA\_KEY\_PRIV, either directly or through the WSCA/WSCD where the key is stored there. The signed nonce is returned to the Provider and verified using WIA\_KEY\_PUB.

During KAs authentication the following steps are executed:

- TOE sends a signed KA(s) to the Provider.
- The Provider verifies the signatures using the Wallet Provider public (WP\_SIG\_PUB1) key. Trust in the Provider's public key shall be established through the applicable Trust List or LoTE.
- The Provider verifies the validity and revocation status of the KA.
- The Provider requires proof-of-possession from the Wallet Unit, of the private counterpart (PID/ATT\_PRIV\_KEY) of the public key in the KA (PID/ATT\_PUB\_KEYs), as

defined in OpenID4VCI. For this, the Provider provides a nonce to the TOE. The TOE will request the WSCA/WSCD to sign this nonce with the PID/ATT\_PRIV\_KEY. The signed nonce is returned to the Provider and the Provider will verify the signature with PID/ATT\_PUB\_KEY from the KAs.

- To avoid a second request from the TOE to the WSCA/WSCD, If the TOE generates a new KA during PID/Attestation issuance the nonce can be included in the KA, and the KA is additionally signed by the PID/ATT\_PRIV\_KEYs matching the public keys in the KA (PID/ATT\_PUB\_KEYs).

The TOE sends a KA to a PID Provider or Attestation Provider only for device-bound, not for non-device-bound PIDs/Attestations.

##### 1.3.3.3 PID/Attestation Generation {#s-1-3-3-3}

Now that the Provider has ensured that it is interacting with the Wallet Unit holding the private key corresponding to the public key embedded in the KA, has verified the applicable WSCA/WSCD security properties, and has verified the Wallet Instance through the WIA, it can generate the PID or Attestation.

For a device-bound PID or Attestation, the Provider binds the issued credential to one of the public keys contained in the applicable KA. The issued PID/Attestation is signed using the Provider's private signing key (ISS\_SIG\_PRIV) and is sent to the TOE using the OpenID4VCI Credential Response.

The exact cryptographic structure of the issued PID or Attestation depends on the credential format and the applicable technical specification.

The Wallet Unit supports, where applicable:

- SD-JWT VC for remote presentation to Relying Parties.
- ISO/IEC 18013-5 mdoc for proximity presentation.

Both formats support selective disclosure based on a common high-level cryptographic principle: the credential contains cryptographic commitments, typically in the form of salted hashes, that allow individual attributes to be disclosed and subsequently verified without disclosing the other attributes. The disclosed attribute and the corresponding cryptographic information allow the Relying Party to verify that the attribute was included in the credential and protected by the Provider's signature.

The detailed cryptographic structures and verification mechanisms are format-specific and are defined by the applicable SD-JWT VC and ISO/IEC 18013-5 specifications.

For device-bound credentials, the public key associated with the protected private key is included or referenced in the credential in accordance with the applicable credential format. During presentation, the Wallet Unit uses the corresponding private key to provide the required proof of possession or device binding.

#### 1.3.4 Credential (PIDs/Attestation) Disclosure {#s-1-3-4}

At this point in the lifecycle, the TOE holds PIDs or Attestations and is ready to disclose selected attributes/claims to the Relying Party.

PIDs/Attestation selective disclosure includes the following steps:

- The TOE authenticates the Relying Party.
- The TOE requests User approval of the attributes/claims to be disclosed and performs selective disclosure.

##### 1.3.4.1 TOE authenticates Relying Party {#s-1-3-4-1}

The TOE authenticates the Relying Party using an Access Certificate (RP\_ACC\_CERT) and obtains or verifies the applicable Relying Party registration information using a Registration Certificate (RP\_REG\_CERT) or the applicable Registrar's online service.

Trust in the Access Certificate and Registration Certificate is established using the applicable trusted anchors.

The Access Certificate is used to authenticate the Relying Party or intermediary participating in the presentation transaction. The Registration Certificate or Registrar service provides information about the Relying Party's registered role, Service, intended use and applicable information relevant to the presentation request.

The TOE must inform the User of the outcome of the Relying Party authentication and certificate validation.

##### 1.3.4.2 User approval and selective disclosure {#s-1-3-4-2}

Prior to User approval, the TOE shall authenticate the User using OS-level or WSCD/WSCAbased authentication.

The TOE shall present the following information to the User and obtain explicit approval before disclosure:

- The identity of the Relying Party, and intermediary parties if present.
- Attributes/claims the Relying Party requested
- Relying Party's intended use (from Registration cert or service), and privacy policy for these attributes,
- Outcome of the evaluation of the requested attributes

The TOE shall support selective disclosure using the mechanism defined by the applicable PID/Attestation format. At a high level, the individual attributes are represented by salted cryptographic hashes that are protected by the Provider's signature. When an attribute is disclosed, the Relying Party can use the disclosed attribute and the corresponding hash information to verify that it was included in the credential, without requiring disclosure of the other attributes.

The TOE shall generate a presentation bound to the transaction, including the freshness value provided by the Relying Party, and use the WSCD/WSCA to sign the presentation with the corresponding PID/Attestation private key (PID/ATT\_PRIV\_KEY). This provides proof-ofpossession of the private key.

The Relying Party shall verify the presentation, including its authenticity, integrity, freshness and the authenticity of the Provider, using the applicable credential and presentation specifications. Trust in the Provider's public key shall be established through the applicable Trust List or LoTE.

After the transaction, the TOE shall enable the User to report unlawful or suspicious requests for personal data and to request deletion of personal data from the Relying Party.

##### 1.3.4.3 Pseudonyms {#s-1-3-4-3}

The TOE shall support the generation and use of pseudonyms for interactions with Relying Parties where required or selected by the User.

Pseudonyms shall be unique and unlinkable across different Relying Parties unless the User explicitly chooses otherwise. The TOE shall securely store and manage the information required to use the pseudonyms and shall prevent disclosure of the User's real-world identity through the pseudonym.

The User shall be able to manage and delete pseudonyms through the Wallet Unit.

#### 1.3.5 Revocation/Deletion {#s-1-3-5}

The Wallet Provider must revoke the Wallet Unit upon explicit User request, upon an explicit request from a PID Provider in accordance with the applicable revocation procedure, and when a security breach or compromise affects the trustworthiness or reliability of the Wallet Unit.

The Wallet Provider must regularly verify that the security of the Wallet Unit is not breached or compromised. This includes the security of the Wallet Instance, the mobile device and OS, and the WSCA/WSCD used to manage critical cryptographic assets. When a security breach or compromise is detected, the Wallet Provider must analyse its cause and impact and, where the trustworthiness or reliability of the Wallet Unit is affected, revoke the Wallet Instance. Where the compromise affects a WSCA/WSCD, the Wallet Provider must also revoke the corresponding WSCA/WSCD.

A Wallet Instance is revoked by setting the revoked status at all index positions specified in the WIAs issued to that Wallet Instance. A WSCD is revoked by setting the revoked status at all index positions specified in the corresponding KAs.

For a revocable PID, the PID Provider must regularly verify the revocation status of the associated Wallet Instance and WSCD using the WIA and KA received during issuance. If either has been revoked, the PID Provider must revoke the corresponding PID. An Attestation Provider may apply a similar procedure to revocable attestations in accordance with its published revocation policy.

The Wallet Unit shall support secure deletion of its contents through a factory reset. This shall delete all attestations, logs, personal data, settings and configurations and, where connected, request the associated WSCA/WSCD to delete the cryptographic assets related to the Wallet Unit.

#### 1.3.6 Additional Wallet Instance Security Functionality {#s-1-3-6}

In addition to the core lifecycle and trust relationships, the Wallet Unit provides the following security-relevant functionality for specific use cases and operational scenarios.

##### 1.3.6.1 Qualified Electronic Signature and Seal {#s-1-3-6-1}

The Wallet shall support the creation of qualified electronic signatures and seals using a local or remote QSCD. The Wallet authenticates the User and obtains explicit approval for the signing operation before securely requesting the signature. For a remote QSCD, the Wallet communicates with the authorized QTSP through a protected channel. A PID or attestation may be used to establish or verify the User’s identity where required but is not inherently required for authorization of the signing operation. The resulting signature is returned to the Wallet and the transaction is recorded.

##### 1.3.6.2 Wallet-to-Wallet (W2W) {#s-1-3-6-2}

The Wallet Unit supports secure Wallet-to-Wallet interactions between Wallet Units. The W2W interaction establishes an authenticated and protected communication channel and requires User awareness and approval before attributes or electronic attestations are disclosed. The interaction protects the exchanged information and transaction against eavesdropping, modification, replay and transaction manipulation.

##### 1.3.6.3 Migration {#s-1-3-6-3}

The Wallet Unit supports secure migration of Wallet Unit contents to a new Wallet Instance. The migration process uses a protected Migration Object containing the information required to restore or re-issue applicable credentials while excluding sensitive information such as WIA, KA and private keys. The Migration Object is protected during creation, storage, export, import and processing against unauthorized disclosure, modification, replacement and replay.

##### 1.3.6.4 DPA Reporting {#s-1-3-6-4}

The Wallet Unit provides the User with a function to report suspicious or inappropriate Relying Party presentation requests to the competent Data Protection Authority (DPA). The function allows the User to identify the relevant Relying Party and transaction and to provide information supporting the complaint.

##### 1.3.6.5 Trust Mark {#s-1-3-6-5}

The Wallet Instance displays the official EUDI Wallet Trust Mark and associated certification information to the User. The Trust Mark information is obtained from the Wallet Provider and protected against unauthorized modification.

##### 1.3.6.6 Logging as an Explicit Lifecycle/Security Function {#s-1-3-6-6}

The Wallet Unit maintains transaction logs covering security-relevant Wallet activities, including issuance, presentation, W2W interactions and electronic signing or sealing transactions. The logs are protected against unauthorized access, modification and deletion and shall not unnecessarily contain the actual values of presented attributes. The wallet instance also supports User access to the logs and recording of relevant DPA reports. This provides traceability of security-relevant Wallet Unit operations throughout the lifecycle.

The WI(TOE) shall protect these assets against unauthorized disclosure, modification, destruction, misuse, replay, substitution, and other security violations that may be attempted by the threat actors.

The required protection of the assets will be ensured by both measures implemented by the WI-(TOE) and measures implemented by the entities in the ecosystem of the WI-(TOE).

### 2.2 Threat model {#s-2-2}

The Wallet solution shall counter the following threats, described in Table 2. These threats describe the primary security risks associated with user impersonation and unauthorized disclosure of Personal Data during presentation.

Table 2 — Primary Threats

| Threat ID                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| T.USER_IMPERSONATI ON       | An attacker presents a stolen or otherwise obtained PID or Attestation to a Relying Party, including a freshly generated and validly signed nonce, in order to impersonate the legitimate Wallet User without the involvement or authorization of the legitimate User.    |
| T.LEAKED_PRESENTAT ION_DATA | An attacker causes Personal Data contained in a Wallet Unit to be disclosed to a Relying Party or other unauthorized recipient without the knowledge and authorization of the legitimate Wallet User, including by manipulating or compromising the presentation process. |

These two threats do not have the same security impact:

- T.USER\_IMPERSONATION is considered the more severe threat, since a successful attack allows an attacker to act as the legitimate Wallet User and to generate a valid Proof-of-Possession for a stolen or otherwise obtained PID or Attestation.
- T.LEAKED\_PRESENTATION\_DATA addresses unauthorized disclosure of Personal Data during the presentation process. Although this threat can have significant privacy consequences, it does not necessarily provide the attacker with the ability to impersonate the User.

The evaluation shall place greater focus on the assets and requirements covering T.USER\_IMPERSONATION, as this threat has a higher security impact than T.LEAKED\_PRESENTATION\_DATA. The requirements mitigating T.LEAKED\_PRESENTATION\_DATA shall also be evaluated, but with a more limited focus.

Section 2.6 identifies which requirements and assets contribute to the mitigation of each threat and its associated attack scenarios identified in Section 2.3.

### 2.3 Attack scenarios {#s-2-3}

Table 3 describes the attack scenarios considered to achieve the T.USER\_IMPERSONATION.

Table 3 — Attack scenario for T.USER\_IMPERSONATION.

| Attack scenarios                                             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|--------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| AS.UI.01 — Fake WSCA/WSCD during channel establishment       | Manipulate the enrolment or establishment of the secure channel between the Wallet Instance and the WSCA/WSCD so that the Wallet Instance connects to an attacker-controlled WSCA/WSCD. The attacker uses stolen or compromised Wallet Provider signing keys to generate or sign fraudulent WIA/KA information, causing the resulting attestation information to appear legitimate. |
| AS.UI.02 — Cloning of Wallet Instance authentication factors | Obtain or compromise both the possession factor and knowledge factor (PIN) used for WSCA/WSCD authentication. The attacker uses the stolen factors to gain control of the Wallet Instance and establish the required authenticated channel to the WSCA/WSCD, allowing the attacker to perform security-sensitive Wallet Unit operations.                                             |
| AS.UI.03 — Theft of device-bound private key                 | Obtain the private key corresponding to a public key bound to a PID or Attestation. The attacker uses the private key to generate a fresh and valid proof of possession for a Relying Party, allowing a stolen or copied PID/Attestation to be presented without the involvement of the legitimate Wallet User.                                                                      |
| AS.UI.04 — Bypass of User authentication                     | Exploit or manipulate the Wallet Instance to bypass OS-level User authentication or the WSCA/WSCD-level Remote User Authentication Protocol (RUAP). The attacker then causes protected cryptographic operations to be performed without the involvement or authorization of the legitimate Wallet User.                                                                              |
| AS.UI.05 — Manipulation of WIA/KA binding                | Manipulate the WIA or KA, so that attacker-controlled keys are presented as belonging to the legitimate Wallet Unit. The attacker subsequently uses the corresponding private key to generate a valid proof of possession during credential presentation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| AS.UI.06 — Replay or manipulation of authentication data | Capture, replay, or manipulate authentication information exchanged between the Wallet Instance and WSCA/WSCD in an attempt to establish an authenticated session or obtain authorization for a security-sensitive cryptographic operation without the legitimate User's involvement.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| AS.UI.07 — Bypass via Migration                          | Exploit weaknesses in the Wallet migration or restore process to transfer Wallet data or credentials to an attacker-controlled or insufficiently authenticated Wallet Instance. The attacker bypasses the required User authentication, source-instance authorization, or destination-instance verification and obtains access to a migrated PID/Attestation or the associated device-bound private key. The attacker can then use the credential and key to generate a valid Proof-of-Possession and impersonate the legitimate Wallet User. |

Table 4 describes the attack scenarios considered to achieve the T.LEAKED\_PRESENTATION\_DATA.

|-------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| AS.LPD.01 — Fake Relying Party                        | Manipulate or replace the Relying Party authentication information so that the Wallet Instance accepts an attacker-controlled or unauthorized entity as the legitimate Relying Party. The attacker then requests Personal Data from the Wallet Instance and causes the User to disclose data to the attacker.                                   |
| AS.LPD.02 — Manipulation of presentation request      | Manipulate the presentation request between the Relying Party and Wallet Instance to alter the requested attributes or claims. The attacker causes the Wallet Instance to request or disclose additional Personal Data that was not originally requested or authorized by the User.                                                             |
| AS.LPD.03 — Bypass of User approval                   | Compromise or manipulate the Wallet Instance to bypass the required User authentication and explicit approval before presentation. The attacker causes the Wallet Instance to perform selective disclosure and generate a presentation without the User knowingly authorizing the disclosure.                                                   |
| AS.LPD.04 — Manipulation of User approval information | Manipulate the information presented to the User during the approval process, such that the User is shown an incomplete or incorrect representation of the Relying Party, requested attributes, intended use, or privacy information. The User consequently authorizes a presentation containing Personal Data that was not knowingly approved. |
| AS.LPD.06 — Manipulation of selective disclosure      | Manipulate the Wallet Instance or presentation processing so that attributes other than those explicitly selected and approved by the User are included in the presentation. The resulting presentation remains cryptographically valid but contains Personal Data beyond the User's intended disclosure.                                       |
| AS.LPD.07 — Presentation data interception            | Intercept Personal Data during the presentation process between the Wallet Instance and the Relying Party or an intermediary. The attacker obtains the disclosed attributes by compromising or manipulating the communication channel or presentation interfaces.                                                                               |
| AS.LPD.08 — Replay or transaction manipulation        | Capture or manipulate information from a presentation transaction and attempt to reuse it in another transaction or with another Relying Party. The attacker attempts to cause Personal Data to be disclosed outside the transaction that was explicitly approved by the User.                                                                  |

Table 6 identifies the security objectives applicable to the subjects and external entities in the operational environment of the Wallet Instance. These objectives define the security activities and responsibilities that support the secure operation of the Wallet Unit, the protection of cryptographic assets, and the establishment and maintenance of the required trust relationships.

|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| OE.WP        | Wallet Provider Trust and Lifecycle Management The Wallet Provider shall establish, maintain and protect the trust relationship with the Wallet Instance throughout its lifecycle. • Securely activate the Wallet Instance and associate it with the appropriate Wallet Provider account. • Establish the required communication and cryptographic trust relationships. • Issue the WIA and KA required for Wallet Unit operations. • Sign the WIA and KA using the Wallet Provider signing key. • Ensure the Wallet Provider signing key is verifiable through the applicable trusted-anchor certificate chain. • Maintain Wallet Instance validity and revocation status and revoke a compromised Wallet Instance. • Protect the integrity and authenticity of information used by PID and Attestation Providers to establish trust in the Wallet Instance |
| OE.WSCA/WSCD | Protection of Cryptographic Assets and Secure Cryptographic Services The WSCA/WSCD shall protect the Wallet Unit's security-critical cryptographic assets and provide a trusted and secure cryptographic service to the Wallet Instance.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| OE.PROVIDER | • Protect security-critical Wallet Unit cryptographic assets, including PID/Attestation private keys and, where applicable, the WIA device-binding private key. • Establish an authenticated and protected communication channel with the Wallet Instance, providing confidentiality and integrity protection against eavesdropping, modification and manipulation. • Perform security-sensitive cryptographic operations only through the established secure channel and following the required User authentication and authorization. • Protect authentication and cryptographic operations against unauthorized use, disclosure, modification, replay and manipulation. • Provide proof-of-possession operations without exposing the protected private keys. • Limit the number of User authentication attempts: keep a failure counter for each User that the Wallet Instance cannot reset. Block the use of protected cryptographic assets after a defined number of consecutive failed verifications and apply increasing delays between attempts before that. • Unblock only after a successful reset procedure (e.g. recovery using PUK). Apply this limit to every verification of User Authentication Evidence, so that the knowledge factor cannot be guessed online through the WSCA/WSCD. • Per-key authorisation data is generated by the WSCD during key generation, is sent to the wallet instance and afterwards provided with each operation. The per-key authorization data will be securely deleted by the WSCA when its no longer needed by the WSCA. PID/Attestation Issuance and Wallet Unit Trust The PID/Attestation Provider shall establish trust in the Wallet Unit and securely bind issued credentials to the verified Wallet Unit cryptographic keys. • Authenticate to the Wallet Instance using the applicable access certificate and registration certificate. • Verify the WIA and KA for authenticity, validity and revocation status using the applicable trust framework. |
| OE.RP       | • For device-bound credentials, verify proof of possession of the private key corresponding to the public key contained in the KA. • Bind the issued PID or Attestation to the verified public key. • Sign issued PIDs and Attestations using the applicable Provider signing key. • Ensure the Provider signing key and issued credentials can be validated through the applicable trusted-anchor certificate chain. Presentation Verification and Transaction Trust The Relying Party shall establish trust in the presentation and verify that the presented Personal Data and associated credentials are valid for the transaction. • Authenticate to the Wallet Instance using the applicable access certificate and registration certificate. • Verify the authenticity, integrity and freshness of each presentation. • Verify the applicable PID/Attestation Provider signature using the applicable trusted-anchor certificate chain. • For device-bound credentials, verify proof of possession of the private key associated with the presented credential. • Accept and process only Personal Data validly presented and authorized for the applicable transaction.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| OE.QTSP              | Protected Qualified Signature and Seal Services The QTSP/Remote QSCD shall provide protected qualified signature or seal services and ensure that signing operations are performed only as authorized by the User. • Protect qualified signing keys against unauthorized access and use. • Perform qualified signature or seal operations only through the authorized signing service and following the required User authentication and explicit authorization. • Protect communication with the Wallet Instance against unauthorized disclosure and manipulation. • Securely return the resulting qualified signature or seal to the Wallet Instance.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| OE.USER_DEVICE       | Secure User Device Platform The User Device on which the Wallet Instance is installed shall provide a hardware-supported security platform with an operating system that still receives security updates. The Wallet Provider shall support the Wallet Instance only on User Devices that meet these conditions: • Provide a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) or Secure Element (SE) offering an isolated execution and storage environment for security-relevant Wallet Instance assets. • Provide a hardware-backed keystore, implemented in the TEE or SE, in which keys are generated, stored and used without the private key material being exported, cloned or exposed to the operating system or other applications. • Enforce key-usage restrictions, including binding key use to User authentication where requested by the Wallet Instance. • Provide key and device attestation giving authentic evidence of the properties of protected keys and the security state of the device. • Provide a trusted boot mechanism so that only authenticated and authorised firmware and operating-system components run with privileged access. • Enforce application sandboxing, process isolation and permission controls between the Wallet Instance and other applications. • Provide OS-level User authentication based on possession of the device combined with a knowledge-based or inherence-based factor. • Receive security updates from the device or OS manufacturer for the period during which the Wallet Provider supports the device |
| OE.APP_DISTRIBUTIO N | Authentic Distribution and Update of the Wallet Instance The Wallet Provider shall distribute the Wallet Instance and all its updates only through channels that preserve their authenticity and integrity: • Distribute the Wallet Instance and its updates through the official application distribution channel of the User Device operating system, or through another mechanism with equivalent protection that lets the User verify the authenticity and integrity of the package before installation. • Sign every release with a Wallet Provider signing key protected against unauthorised use and disclosure. • Ensure that the package signature is verified before the Wallet Instance is installed or updated, and that updates are accepted only when signed by the same signing identity as the installed version. • Release only versions covered by the applicable certification or certification maintenance process. • Provide security updates in a timely manner when vulnerabilities affecting the Wallet Instance are identified. • Define a minimum supported version and prevent older versions from being used for security-sensitive operations, for example by refusing to issue a WIA to them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

### 2.6 Coverage of the Security Requirements {#s-2-6}

Chapter 3 provides the complete set of detailed security requirements, including the Functional Security Requirements (FSRs) and Resilience Security Requirements (RSRs). The FSRs are derived from the ARF and applicable regulations, while the RSRs provide additional resilience and robustness measures for the Wallet Instance.

#### 2.6.1 Coverage of the Life Cycle {#s-2-6-1}

Appendix A.1 provides the coverage mapping between the security requirements and the relevant life-cycle sections defined in section 1.3. The mapping demonstrates that the security-relevant activities throughout the Wallet Instance life cycle are addressed by the identified FSRs.

#### 2.6.2 Coverage of the Threats {#s-2-6-2}

This section identifies the assets, Functional Security Requirements (FSRs), Resilience Security Requirements (RSRs), and Environmental Security Objectives that contribute to the mitigation of the two threats defined for the Wallet Instance. The coverage is based on the attack scenarios identified in Appendix A.2.

##### 2.6.2.1 Requirements and Assets covering T.USER\_IMPERSONATION {#s-2-6-2-1}

The primary objective for T.USER\_IMPERSONATION is to ensure that an attacker cannot successfully act as the legitimate Wallet User by presenting a PID or Attestation together with a valid Proof-of-Possession. Table 7 gives a coverage assessment for T.USER\_IMPERSONATION.

Table 7 — Coverage for T.USER\_IMPERSONATION

| Assets and Requirements          | Coverage                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|----------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Assets                           | The assets that require particular protection for this threat are A.WIID, A.PIN, A.PUK, A.KEYAUTH, A.POSS, A.UAE and A.ARD, which together support the User authentication mechanism; A.MUT_KEY and A.CMD, which protect the authenticated communication and security-sensitive WSCA/WSCD operations; A.WIA and A.KA, which establish trust in the Wallet Instance and its cryptographic keys; A.PIDATT, which contains the credentials used for identification; and A.NONCE, which provides freshness for proof and presentation transactions. A.MIGR is used to perform secure migration.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Functional Security Requirements | The threat is mitigated through the combined protection of FSR_WI_INSTALL, FSR_SEC_CHANNEL, FSR_LOCAL_AUTH, FSR_REMOTE_AUTH and FSR_WIA, FSR_MIGRATION. FSR_WI_INSTALL and FSR_WIA and FSR_KEY_ATTEST ensure that the Wallet Instance and its cryptographic bindings are established and verified every 24h. FSR_SEC_CHANNEL protects channel establishment and authentication exchanges against interception, replay and manipulation, while FSR_LOCAL_AUTH and FSR_REMOTE_AUTH prevent authentication bypass and require the legitimate User to authorize security-sensitive operations. Together, these measures prevent an attacker from establishing a connection with a fraudulent WSCA/WSCD, using cloned authentication factors, or using compromised device-bound keys or manipulated authentication/binding data to impersonate the legitimate User. FSR_MIGRATION ensures that migration from one wallet instance to an other wallet instance is properly secured. |
| Resilience Security Requirements | The collective RSRs in section 3.2 mitigate this threat by maintaining the security of the Wallet Instance, its authentication factors, cryptographic keys, execution environment and security-sensitive interactions even in the presence of active attacks or a compromised execution environment. They prevent unauthorized extraction or cloning of device-bound keys and authentication data, detect compromised or manipulated device and software states, protect sensitive authentication input and communications, and prevent security-critical operations when the required security state or integrity cannot be established. This collectively limits the ability to substitute or manipulate the Wallet Instance, obtain the factors or keys required for authentication, bypass user interaction, or use compromised components to perform operations as the legitimate User.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Environmental Objectives         | The environmental objectives are particularly important for this threat because the Wallet Instance does not itself provide all of the required security functionality. OE.USER protects the User's authentication factors and requires the User to retain control of them. OE.WP establishes and maintains the trust relationship with the Wallet Provider and protects the WIA/KA issuance chain. OE.WSCA/WSCD protects the security-critical private keys and provides the cryptographic operations required to generate Proof-of- Possession without exposing those private keys. OE.PROVIDER verifies the WIA, KA and Proof-of-Possession and binds issued credentials to the verified public key. Finally, OE.RP verifies the authenticity of the credential and the Proof-of-Possession during presentation. These environmental responsibilities are explicitly defined in the Protection Profile. OE.USER_DEVICE mandates minimum security related requirements for the underlying hardware. Furthermore, OE.APP_DISTRIBUTION mandates a secure application distribution channel. |

##### 2.6.2.2 Requirements and Assets covering T.LEAKED\_PRESENTATION\_DATA {#s-2-6-2-2}

T.LEAKED\_PRESENTATION\_DATA has a different and narrower security objective. Here, the attacker does not necessarily need to impersonate the User. The threat is that Personal Data contained in the Wallet Unit is disclosed to an RP or another recipient without the User's knowledge and authorization. Table 8 gives a coverage assessment T.LEAKED\_PRESENTATION\_DATA.

Table 8 — Coverage for T.LEAKED\_PRESENTATION\_DATA

|----------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Assets                           | The principal assets for this threat are A.PIDATT, because it contains the Personal Data-bearing PIDs and Attestations; A.PRES, because it contains the presentation data generated for a transaction; A.CERT, because RP access and registration certificates establish the identity and authorization of the RP; A.ANCHOR, because trust anchors are required to validate the associated certificates and signed objects; and A.NONCE, because freshness data binds the presentation to the intended transaction and prevents replay.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Functional Security Requirements | The core FSRs for this threat are consequently FSR_TRUST_ANCHOR, FSR_ACC_REG_CERT, FSR_SELECT_DISCLO, FSR_PRESENTATION, FSR_PROTOCOL FSR_DATA_DELETION and FSR_MDOC. FSR_TRUST_ANCHOR and FSR_ACC_REG_CERT ensures that the RP is authenticated and that its access and registration information is valid before disclosure. It also ensures that the RP or service information presented to the User corresponds to the authenticated entity. FSR_SELECT_DISCLO is the central requirement for this threat because it ensures that only attributes explicitly approved by the User are included in the presentation. FSR_PROTOCOL ensures that the presentation request, User approval and resulting presentation remain associated with the same transaction and are protected against manipulation and replay. FSR_PRESENTATION ensures that only valid credentials are presented, while FSR_MDOC provides the corresponding protection for mdoc presentations. FSR_DATA_DELETION ensures that presentation data is properly deleted. |
